headline: Malawi Launches Free Orthopaedic Care Programme for 900 Children
meta_description: Malawi is launching a three-year programme to provide free orthopaedic surgery and mobility aids to 900 children with disabilities.
summary_short: Malawi begins a three-year initiative offering free orthopaedic care, surgery, and mobility aids to 900 children with disabilities in two regions.
body:
Malawi is launching a three-year programme to provide free orthopaedic care, including surgery and mobility aids, to 900 children with disabilities. The initiative will serve families in Lilongwe and Mzimba North, giving children access to treatments that were previously out of reach for many families in the region.

Orthopaedic disabilities often limit children's mobility and independence, affecting their ability to attend school and participate in daily life. By combining surgical intervention with mobility aids—such as wheelchairs, braces, and assistive devices—the programme addresses both immediate medical needs and long-term quality of life.

The three-year commitment signals a sustained effort to transform healthcare access for vulnerable children across two key regions. For families in Lilongwe and Mzimba North, the programme offers hope that disability will no longer be a barrier to care.
quick_facts: 900 children with disabilities to receive free orthopaedic care
Three-year programme in Lilongwe and Mzimba North, Malawi
Includes surgery and mobility aids for improved mobility
